For a circular loop carrying current, the magnetic field at the center is perpendicular to the plane of the loop (along the axis).  
Around each small portion of the wire, the magnetic field lines form concentric circles around that portion, so at any point just outside the wire, the magnetic field is tangential to such a circle — meaning it is perpendicular to the radius from the center of the loop, i.e., perpendicular to the circumference of the wire at that point.  

Final answer: (B)
